newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI CHUGS AHEAD, NOKIA AND FORESTRIES LEAD.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI CHUGS AHEAD, NOKIA AND FORESTRIES LEAD.

text.p: Finnish shares rose steadily
across the board on Monday in moderate trade with U.S. stocks
adding to Friday's gains as Wall Street opened, and gains in
Nokia and forestries cheered sentiment, brokers said.
Activity in Helsinki and other European bourses was muted
with London and Tokyo closed for holidays, bur the German DAX
index managed a new record. Total volume in Helsinki was 447
million markka of which Nokia accounted for 34 percent.
The HEX general index rose 0.84 to 2,997.57 points and the
FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark was up 0.92 percent at
1,041.10, just a whisker off its 1,042.81 point session high.
The HEX was seen testing the 3,000-point mark again on
Tuesday. "With London open -- I think we might see more gains
tomorrow," one broker said.
"This looks like a good week, unless anything appears to
disturb the positive market sentiment," said another.
Nokia ended up 3.00 markka at 331.00, 1.00 markka off its
intra-session high.
The forest industry sub-index rose 0.29 percent although
UPM-Kymmene fell 0.50 markka to 120.50. Metsa-Serla and Enso
advanced strongly, helped by gains in Swedish forestry shares
and more favourable prospects for the sector, brokers said.
Finnish options exchange SOP's Pulp Indicator Index put the value of northern bleached softwood pulp at $524.55 per
tonne, up from last week's $519.18, boosting hopes that the key
price trend indicator for paper products was recovering.
"The pulp news was good news since it was the first real
increase in quite a while," one broker said.
Electronics and furniture subcontractor Incap ended its
first day on the OTC list at 51.00 markka, six markka up from
its 44 markka offering price. "Like all the other new shares on
the list this year, Incap attracted quite a bit of interest and
was well received," one broker said.

Oil group Neste rose 5.00 markka or almost four percent in fair trade after its petrochemicals group Borealis, co-owned with Norwegian Statoil , posted a sharp rise in its Q1 profits, exceeding expectations, brokers said.
Steel group Rautaruukki was lively, staying well above its recent 42.00 markka offering price as it added 0.20 markka to 47.30 in healthy almost 22 million markka volume.
Metra rose 1.00 markka to 144.00 in lively 28 million markka trade on interest in metal and engineering stocks, brokers said.
